{"markdown":"# Issues Memo — Master Services Agreement (RadialSpark / Clear Capital)

**To:** Deal team
**From:** In-house counsel (Customer-side)
**Re:** Playbook review — verified findings

---

## 1. Executive summary

We reviewed the Agreement against the playbook and recorded 18 findings: 7 compliant, 7 deviations, 3 missing clauses and 1 item requiring further review. The commercial architecture is favourable to us in several respects — deliverable ownership vests in the Company, there is no exclusivity, no minimum commitment, no MFN, no non-compete, no liquidated damages and no auto-renewal — so our redlines are targeted rather than wholesale.

Three issues drive the negotiation. First, there is **no indemnity anywhere in the document** despite the Section 7 heading promising one; the sole carve-out from the liability cap cross-refers to Paragraph 9, which is the Independent Contractor clause, so the exception is illusory. Second, the **liability cap** is a per-SOW, fees-paid-only cap with no carve-outs for indemnity, confidentiality, IP infringement, gross negligence or wilful misconduct. Third, the insurance schedule carries **no cyber/privacy cover** even though Contractor handles Company data and accesses Company systems. Two of these (absence of Vendor IP indemnity; zero cyber cover) sit in walk-away territory under the playbook.

Secondary asks are: a Company termination-for-convenience right (today we cannot exit an open-ended, active engagement except for breach), post-termination transition assistance and data return (absent entirely), a 90-day deliverable conformity warranty with a real remedy, an affiliate/successor assignment carve-out, a general-advertising carve-out to the mutual non-solicit, and a move of governing law from Arizona to an accepted jurisdiction.

---

## 2. Findings

| Severity | Rule | Status | Section | Summary |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| Critical | INDEMN — Indemnification by Vendor | Missing | § 7 (Limitations of Liability; Indemnification of Contractor) | Heading promises indemnification but no operative indemnity or hold-harmless exists; § 5(c) gives a bare non-infringement warranty only, capped under § 7(a). Insert Contractor indemnity as new § 7(d), carved out of the cap. |
| Critical | IP — Ownership of deliverables and Customer Data | Compliant | § 4 (Ownership of Materials; Acceptance) | Works vest in Company with perfection assistance; Contractor pre-existing IP paired with a royalty-free, perpetual, sublicensable licence back. Meets preferred position; minor gaps (no "irrevocable"/"worldwide"; ownership on invoice "paid" rather than paid or payable) noted only. |
| Critical | LOL-CAP — Limitation of liability | Deviation | § 7 | Per-SOW fees-paid cap below the fallback 12-month mutual cap; sole carve-out cross-refers to Paragraph 9 (Independent Contractor), so no effective carve-outs. Raise to greater of 12 months' fees and USD 1,000,000 and add mutual uncapped Excluded Claims. |
| High | ASSIGN — Assignment and change of control | Deviation | § 7 (clause at § 10) | Symmetrical consent with no affiliate/successor carve-out, so all Company M&A and internal reorganisations need Contractor consent. Add carve-out on notice, bar assignment to our competitors, confirm change of control is not a deemed assignment. |
| High | EXCLUSIVITY — Exclusivity binding Customer | Compliant | § 1 (Purpose of Engagement) | Task-by-task SOW structure, no sole-source or requirements commitment. Preferred position; no redline. |
| High | LD — Liquidated damages / penalties payable by Customer | Compliant | § 6 (Termination) | Termination obligates us only to pay fees earned through the effective date; no kill fee, penalty or minimum. Preferred position. |
| High | LICENSE — Licence grant scope | Needs review | § 4 | Assessed as sitting at the fallback (perpetual, sublicensable, consent-not-unreasonably-withheld transfer route), so no redline proposed — **but verification did not pass and this item should be re-confirmed before we sign off.** |
| High | NONCOMPETE — Non-compete on Customer | Compliant | § 4 | No non-compete, field-of-use or territory restriction on Company; § 13 is a mutual personnel non-solicit and p0020 is an ordinary licence-scope limit. Preferred position. |
| Medium | GOVLAW — Governing law and venue | Deviation | § 7 (clauses at governing law / § 19) | Arizona law is outside the accepted list and there is no venue clause; arbitration confirmation sits in the losing party's district. Move to New York with exclusive New York County jurisdiction and seat arbitration there; Delaware, California, England and Wales remain acceptable. |
| Medium | MFN — Most-favoured-nation burdening Customer | Compliant | § 3 (Contractor's Compensation) | No best-pricing or matching obligation on Company. Preferred position; the 30-day rate-change right is a pricing point, not an MFN. |
| Medium | MINCOMMIT — Minimum commitments / volume restrictions | Compliant | § 3 | Time-and-materials, fees only for Services ordered and performed; no minimum, shortfall or retainer. Note: future SOWs should be screened for minimum hours or retainer floors. |
| Medium | NOSOLICIT — Non-solicitation binding Customer | Deviation | § 7 (clause at § 13) | Mutual, narrowly scoped and 12 months, but no carve-out for general advertising or unsolicited approaches, which the fallback treats as material. Add the standard carve-out sentence. |
| Medium | RENEWAL — Auto-renewal and notice window | Compliant | § 1 | No auto-renewal; term runs until terminated, 15 days' convenience notice when no SOW outstanding. More favourable than preferred. Rate-change right without a cap is noted for the pricing rule. |
| Medium | T4C — Termination for convenience | Deviation | § 6 | Convenience right available only when no SOW is outstanding, against an indefinite term — we cannot exit a live engagement except for breach. Add a 30-day Company convenience right with refund of prepaid fees and no termination fee. |
| Medium | TRANSITION — Transition assistance and data return | Missing | § 6 | No transition assistance, no data or Confidential Information return, no deletion or certification anywhere. Insert as new § 6(c); 90-day window available as fallback. |
| Medium | WARRANTY — Performance warranty and duration | Deviation | § 5 (Representations, Warranties and Disclaimer) | No conformity warranty, period or remedy, and § 5(e) strips implied warranties. Insert a 90-day conformity warranty with repair/replace/refund and a no-malicious-code assurance before the disclaimer. |
| Low | AUDIT — Audit rights against Customer | Missing | § 3 | No audit, inspection or verification clause in either direction. Defensive new § 3(d) confirms Contractor has no audit right and caps any SOW- or law-derived verification (annual, 30 days' notice, independent auditor, off-site only, Contractor's cost unless underpayment exceeds 5%). Finding verification was repaired. |
| Low | INSURANCE — Vendor insurance | Deviation | § 7 (clause at § 14) | Workers' comp, CGL USD 1M, E&O USD 1M and certificates present, but **no cyber/privacy cover of any amount** while Contractor handles Company data and accesses Company systems. Add cyber at USD 5M (fallback USD 2M). Minor items (no CGL aggregate, E&O at fallback, no tail) noted only. |

---

## 3. Walk-away items

The following are identified in the findings as walk-away territory and should be treated as conditions to signature:

1. **No Vendor indemnity (INDEMN, § 7).** The absence of any Vendor IP indemnity is walk-away territory under the rule and fails both the preferred and fallback positions. We require the new § 7(d) Contractor indemnity covering third-party IP infringement, breach of law, data/Confidential Information breach and gross negligence or wilful misconduct, with notice/control/cooperation mechanics and a carve-out from the § 7(a) cap. We have offered a reciprocal Company indemnity narrowed to Company-furnished materials and Company's breach of law.
2. **No cyber/privacy insurance (INSURANCE, § 14).** A vendor that handles our data and touches our systems with zero cyber cover falls in walk-away territory. We ask for cyber/privacy liability at USD 5,000,000, with USD 2,000,000 available as the fallback; the negotiated CGL, E&O, workers' compensation and certificate mechanics are left untouched.

Closely related and effectively part of the same package: the § 7(a) cap and its broken Paragraph 9 cross-reference (LOL-CAP). The indemnity is of limited value unless indemnity, confidentiality, IP infringement, gross negligence and wilful misconduct sit outside the cap.

---

## 4. Next steps

1. **Re-verify the LICENSE finding (§ 4).** Verification failed on this item. Before we conclude that the grant sits at the fallback and needs no redline, we should re-run the analysis. If § 4 or the assignment clause is reopened for other reasons, the low-cost asks are adding "irrevocable", inserting "and its Affiliates and contractors acting on its behalf", and carving M&A successors out of the assignment consent.
2. **Issue the redline** covering: new § 7(d) indemnity and conformed § 7 heading; revised § 7(a) cap with mutual Excluded Claims; new § 6(c) transition assistance, data return and certified deletion; 90-day conformity warranty in § 5; Company 30-day convenience right in § 6; affiliate/successor assignment carve-out; general-advertising and unsolicited-approach carve-outs to § 13; cyber cover in § 14; New York governing law and venue; and defensive § 3(d) on verification.
3. **Sequence the negotiation.** Present the indemnity, cap carve-outs and cyber cover as a single non-negotiable package. Governing law, non-solicit carve-outs and the audit provision are lower-value and can be traded.
4. **Flag for the business team:** (i) § 3(b) permits Contractor to change rates on 30 days' notice with no CPI or percentage cap — a pricing decision for the commercial owner, mitigated by per-SOW fixed rates and our short exit notice; (ii) individual Statements of Work sit outside this document and should be screened for minimum hours, retainer floors and any audit right, noting that § 1(a) gives this Agreement precedence over conflicting SOW terms.
5. **Optional clean-up if the document is otherwise being amended:** add "irrevocable" and "worldwide" to the § 4(c) licence back and change deliverable ownership to attach on fees "paid or payable"."}
